records.Concise description: Standard `bitcoin:` payment URI lineage for encoding payment instructions, with BIP 321 superseding the older BIP 21 specification.
records.Deeper researched summary: BIP 21 established the familiar `bitcoin:` URI used to pass an address, amount and optional parameters to wallet software. BIP 321 modernizes and supersedes that lineage, allowing richer payment instructions and extensibility while retaining the same URI scheme. It is an application/payment interoperability standard, not a custody system or separate payment network, and wallet implementation support for newer fields can vary.
Creators / founders: Bitcoin Improvement Proposal authors and contributors
records.Launch / history: BIP 21 dates to the early Bitcoin payment-URI era; BIP 321 was assigned in 2024 and superseded BIP 21 as the maintained URI specification.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin payments e: It is the basic machine-readable bridge between merchant/payment applications and wallets for on-chain and multi-method Bitcoin payment instructions.
Important technical or cultural characte: Can carry/relate multiple Bitcoin payment instructions
records.Verification basis: Current Bitcoin BIP repository/spec pages identify BIP 321 as Complete and BIP 21 as superseded/closed, supporting one consolidated lineage profile.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not imply every wallet supports every BIP 321 parameter.
This is an application/interoperability standard, not a blockchain or payment processor.
BIP 21 is consolidated here rather than duplicated as a historical profile.

records.Concise description: Collaborative on-chain Bitcoin payment protocol in which sender and receiver jointly construct a transaction so common-input ownership heuristics are less reliable.
records.Deeper researched summary: Payjoin's deployed BIP 78 design lets a receiver contribute inputs and outputs to a payment transaction, breaking the simplistic assumption that all transaction inputs belong to one sender. Newer Payjoin v2 work is specified in draft BIP 77 with asynchronous/store-and-forward transport ideas. These must be distinguished: BIP 78 is deployed, while BIP 77 remains draft as of verification. Payjoin can improve transaction-analysis resistance but does not guarantee anonymity or hide all payment metadata.
Creators / founders: BIP authors and Payjoin open-source contributors
records.Launch / history: BIP 78 was standardized in 2019-era Payjoin development; later Payjoin v2 work moved into draft BIP 77 to improve asynchronous discovery/transport.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin payments e: It is one of Bitcoin's most important payment-specific privacy patterns because privacy improvement happens inside ordinary-looking on-chain payments rather than through a separate asset or chain.
records.Verification basis: Primary BIP specifications verify deployed BIP 78 and the distinct draft status of BIP 77; current project material verifies active Payjoin implementation work.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not call Payjoin anonymous or guaranteed private.
Do not present BIP 77/Payjoin v2 as a finalized universally deployed standard.
Wallet/merchant interoperability must be verified per implementation.

records.Concise description: BIP 352 protocol for reusable static Bitcoin payment addresses that derive unique on-chain Taproot outputs to reduce address reuse and direct payment-linkability.
records.Deeper researched summary: Silent Payments let a recipient publish a static address while senders derive fresh Taproot output keys using transaction inputs and recipient scan/spend keys. The recipient scans relevant transactions to discover payments. The protocol is Complete at the BIP specification level, but that does not mean universal wallet deployment. It is an on-chain payment-addressing/privacy mechanism, not a Lightning system and not a guarantee against all forms of transaction analysis.
records.Launch / history: Developed from earlier reusable-payment-address ideas and standardized as BIP 352 in the 2020s.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin payments e: It tackles the practical problem of reusable payment identifiers without reusing one on-chain address, a major merchant/donation/payment-addressing privacy concern.
Important technical or cultural characte: Fresh Taproot output derivation per payment
Recipient scan key and spend key model
records.Verification basis: Primary BIP specification verifies the protocol design and Complete status.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not equate Complete BIP status with universal deployed wallet support.
Do not promise payment anonymity; Silent Payments address reusable-address linkability, not every network/transaction metadata leak.

records.Entity / project type: Lightning application protocol suite / payment addressing convention
records.Concise description: LNURL application-protocol suite and its Lightning Address convention for discovering Lightning payment requests through web identifiers and service endpoints.
records.Deeper researched summary: LNURL is a set of optional Lightning application protocols documented as LUDs, not part of the core BOLT specification. LUD-06 defines payRequest behavior and LUD-16 describes static internet identifiers; Lightning Address builds the familiar `name@domain` user-facing form on that discovery model. The address is a naming/discovery layer, not the actual custody system or payment transport: the flow ultimately resolves service metadata and obtains Lightning payment instructions such as an invoice.
records.Launch / history: LNURL emerged in the late 2010s/early 2020s to improve Lightning UX for pay, withdraw, auth and related application interactions; Lightning Address became a widely used human-readable receiving convention.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin payments e: It made Lightning payments easier to initiate from reusable, human-readable identifiers without claiming that those identifiers are wallets or a new Lightning protocol layer.
Important technical or cultural characte: Not part of core BOLT specifications
records.Verification basis: Current LNURL specification repository documents the optional LUD suite, payRequest and static internet identifiers and remains actively maintained.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not describe LNURL as a BOLT or as Bitcoin consensus.
Do not call a Lightning Address a wallet, custody system or payment rail by itself.
Support differs by wallet/service because LUDs are optional.
